items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

judge.evidence_topic: Participants read a fictitious news report in which original information and a retraction were each presented by either a source with high credibility or a source with low credibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments ( N = 151, N = 146), informant credibility and retractor credibility were independently manipulated.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental publicado em periódico revisado por pares dentro do período solicitado. O tema (CIE) e o uso de materiais neutros (relatos de notícias fictícias) atendem perfeitamente às restrições do pedido. Os dados extraídos descrevem corretamente o método e os achados principais do resumo.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE). Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) por meio de experimentos com participantes humanos utilizando cenários de eventos neutros, conforme solicitado. O método descrito no resumo (experimentos com fronteiras de segmentação de eventos) está alinhado com a descrição fornecida. O achado principal extraído reflete precisamente os resultados dos experimentos 1 e 2 relatados no resumo.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: We compared the data quality obtained using open and closed response formats using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental publicado em 2018 que investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando um cenário neutro (evento em desdobramento), atendendo a todos os critérios do pesquisador. Os dados extraídos refletem corretamente o conteúdo do resumo.

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation can continue to influence reasoning after correction; this is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico que investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando uma tarefa experimental padrão e medidas de função executiva. O achado principal sobre a capacidade da função executiva em predizer a suscetibilidade ao CIE é sustentado diretamente pelo resumo.

items.title: Effective mitigation of the belief perseverance bias after the retraction of misinformation: Awareness training and counter-speech

judge.evidence_topic: This paper contributes to research on mitigating the belief perseverance bias after the retraction of misinformation by proposing counter-speech and awareness-training techniques and comparing them in terms of effectiveness to the existing counter-explanation technique in an experiment with N = 251 participants.
judge.evidence_empirical: in an experiment with N = 251 participants.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada (belief perseverance bias) e testa técnicas de mitigação em um experimento com participantes humanos. O resumo sustenta o achado de que a técnica de contra-argumentação (CS) é a mais eficaz.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The practical relevance of this work is particularly apparent as we confront fake news everyday.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.reason: O resumo não especifica que os materiais utilizados nos estudos eram neutros ou fictícios, mencionando apenas 'fake news' de forma genérica, o que não permite confirmar o cumprimento da restrição de neutralidade do pedido.

items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) por meio de experimentos, sem abordar temas proibidos (política, saúde, etc.). O resumo sustenta o achado principal e o tamanho da amostra não é mencionado no texto fornecido, conforme corretamente identificado pelos dados extraídos.

items.title: The role of discomfort in the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Research examining the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has reliably found that belief in misinformation persists even after the misinformation has been retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: Studies 1 and 2 found that retractions of misinformation elicit psychological discomfort, and this discomfort predicts continued belief in and use of misinformation. Study 3 showed that the relations between discomfort and continued belief in and use of misinformation are causal in nature by manipulating how participants appraised the meaning of discomfort.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e utiliza experimentos com participantes humanos para testar mecanismos psicológicos (desconforto) em retratações, o que está alinhado com o pedido. O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo. Embora o resumo não mencione explicitamente o cenário de 'incêndio em depósito', o estudo é um experimento sobre CIE, o que é consistente com o pedido.

items.title: The independent effects of source expertise and trustworthiness on retraction believability: The moderating role of vested interest

judge.evidence_topic: Study 1 demonstrated that retractions from an expert source are believed more and lead to less continued belief in misinformation than retractions from an inexpert source while controlling for perceptions of trustworthiness.
judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that retractions from an expert source are believed more and lead to less continued belief in misinformation than retractions from an inexpert source... Study 2 found similar effects using a design containing manipulations of both expertise and trustworthiness.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve dois estudos experimentais que investigam a eficácia de retratações e a crença continuada, utilizando manipulações de variáveis, o que está alinhado com o pedido. O achado principal reflete precisamente o que foi descrito no resumo.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction. This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.evidence_empirical: This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental publicado em 2024 que investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) da desinformação. O resumo confirma a realização de três experimentos e os achados relatados no resumo sustentam integralmente a conclusão extraída.

items.title: Did he or didn't he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions... Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements.
judge.evidence_empirical: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários fictícios neutros, atendendo aos critérios de tema e restrições de conteúdo. O estudo é empírico (três experimentos) e o achado relatado no resumo coincide exatamente com a descrição fornecida nos dados extraídos.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) usando cenários fictícios neutros (formação de impressão de um personagem), o que está alinhado com o pedido. O método descrito (4 experimentos com participantes humanos) é condizente com o resumo. O achado principal de que a desinformação foi totalmente descartada após a retratação é explicitamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Mechanisms in continued influence: The impact of misinformation corrections on source perceptions

judge.evidence_topic: Research on the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has demonstrated that misinformation continues to influence people’s beliefs and judgments even after it has been corrected.
judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that an external correction (i.e., a new source labeling misinformation as false) influences perceptions of the misinformation source, and these perceptions of the misinformation source then correlated with belief in the misinformation. Study 2 replicated the results of Study 1 and used source derogation to manipulate misinformation source perceptions and further lessen continued belief. Study 3 was a preregistered replication of previous results using new methodology.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve três estudos empíricos experimentais sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e mecanismos de correção, utilizando metodologia experimental. O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Combating false information in military situations: Striking the right balance between continued influence effect and overcorrection

judge.evidence_topic: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making... Two of the scenarios presented FI which was later retracted... The results did not reveal any evidence of the CIE, but an overcorrection effect emerged in decision‐making.
judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making, followed by an assessment of their inferential reasoning.
judge.reason: O estudo utiliza cenários militares fictícios, que são neutros e não se enquadram nas exclusões (política, saúde, vacinas, COVID-19). O método (4 cenários, 61 participantes) e o achado (não houve CIE, mas houve supercorreção) estão corretamente descritos e sustentados pelo resumo: 'A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios... The results did not reveal any evidence of the CIE, but an overcorrection effect emerged in decision‐making.'

items.title: I know It's false, but I keep thinking as if it were true: A replication study of Johnson and Seifert's (1994) continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23). The results confirm those of the original study, supporting the validity of Johnson and Seifert's paradigm (1994) and extending its applicability to a French-speaking population.
judge.evidence_empirical: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que replica o experimento 1A de Johnson e Seifert (1994), utilizando um cenário fictício (neutro) para investigar o efeito de influência continuada, atendendo a todos os critérios de inclusão.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando experimentos com cenários fictícios, sem abordar temas proibidos como política ou saúde. O método descrito no resumo condiz com o que foi extraído, e o achado principal é sustentado pela conclusão do resumo de que não houve evidência de que explicar a origem da desinformação fosse mais eficaz do que apenas corrigi-la.

items.title: The neural basis of the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: They were instructed to read brief, fictional news reports and answer three inference questions after reading while lying in a 3.0T Siemens Prisma MRI scanner.
judge.evidence_empirical: Thirty-one participants (10 males) were recruited in this study.
judge.reason: O tamanho da amostra foi informado no resumo (31 participantes), contrariando o dado extraído. Além disso, o achado principal extraído sobre os escores de inferência não é sustentado pelo resumo, que foca nas diferenças de ativação cerebral e conectividade funcional, sem reportar explicitamente que os escores de inferência foram maiores na condição de retratação.

items.title: Failure to accept retractions: A contribution to the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: Previous research has shown that when information about a narrative event is retracted, people continue to use that information... The current study explored whether this effect reflects, at least in part, an unwillingness of some readers to accept changes to their understanding.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiment 1 assessed this using a continued influence effect paradigm... Experiment 2 included... Experiment 3 modified the alternative account to increase plausibility, and added two additional stories/question sets
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) usando narrativas neutras, o que está alinhado com o pedido. O método descrito (3 experimentos, paradigma CIE, histórias narrativas) é condizente com o resumo. O achado principal é sustentado pela conclusão do resumo.

items.title: Reading Medium and Epistemic Emotions in the Continued Influence Effect of Misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: In this study, college students (N = 84) read about fictional news events, each with the first article stating misinformation and the second providing corrected updated information
judge.evidence_empirical: This was a within-subjects experiment in that two events were read on paper and two on screen
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários fictícios neutros, o que está alinhado com o pedido. O estudo é empírico e experimental, com participantes humanos, e o achado extraído reflete fielmente o resultado relatado no resumo.
